content.jointProblem: How should script normalization and transliteration be placed in a PostgreSQL full-text search pipeline so that Latin queries retrieve Cyrillic contracts, Cyrillic queries retrieve Latin contracts, and mixed-script documents remain searchable without noticeable latency increase? We would test index-time, query-time, and combined normalization, including a cascaded deterministic-plus-neural fallback for ambiguous or out-of-vocabulary tokens, against a held-out set of real contract searches.

rationale.text: Dragić has published a mixed-script inverted-index methodology that processes Cyrillic and Latin occurrences without full conversion to one script.

sources.quote: invertovanog indeksa koji istovremeno obrađuje ćirilična i latinična pojavljivanja srpskih reči bez prethodnog potpunog prevođenja u jedno pismo

rationale.text: He has evaluated phoneme-based token canonicalization on a legal corpus and query–document relevance pairs.

sources.quote: We evaluated the approach on a manually annotated gold standard of 4 200 query–document relevance pairs drawn from a legal corpus of 38 000 court decisions.

rationale.text: His query-expansion experiments measured retrieval latency overhead under 12 ms at the 95th percentile.

sources.quote: the overhead introduced by expansion remains under 12 ms at the 95th percentile for queries up to eight tokens.

rationale.text: He has practical pilot experience adding script normalization to internal document search in SMEs.

sources.quote: iskustva iz tri pilot implementacije interne pretrage zasnovane na open-source pretražnom okviru dopunjenom modulom za normalizaciju pisma

rationale.text: He has industry experience adapting a search module for Serbian court decisions for a legaltech startup.

sources.quote: sarađivao je s jednim novosadskim startapom iz oblasti legaltech-a na prilagođavanju pretražnog modula za srpske sudske odluke

rationale.text: He led a work package on script normalization and transliteration in a Serbian–Romanian administrative retrieval project.

sources.quote: Stefan Dragić rukovodi radnim paketom koji pokriva normalizaciju skripte i transliteraciju na srpskoj strani

risks: Most of the researcher's evidence comes from news, court, web, or encyclopedia corpora; transfer to the company's contract corpus and PostgreSQL full-text search is unproven and must be tested first.
The six-week, one-engineer capacity may not be enough to implement, evaluate, and tune index-time/query-time placement plus edge-case rules.
Dialect-dependent Latin-to-Cyrillic ambiguities and foreign loanwords or proper nouns remain error sources; the evidence identifies these as unresolved edge cases.
Actual researcher availability is marked unknown; notes indicate capacity for one smaller industrial contract or consultancy, but this is not confirmed against two active projects.
Company contract corpus size, script mix, and sample-sharing feasibility are unknown, so evaluation feasibility is uncertain.
Changing indexing may require reindexing existing documents; migration and downtime constraints are not stated.
questions: Can Prof. Dragić confirm actual availability and effort level for a joint project given two active projects and the stated capacity for one smaller industrial contract or consultancy?
What is the size of the contract corpus, the share of mixed-script documents, and can a representative anonymized query/document sample be shared for evaluation?
Which PostgreSQL version and full-text search configuration are used, and is reindexing or downtime allowed for an index-time normalization approach?
What latency SLO applies to search, and which historical query log set will be used for before/after evaluation?
Which dialect or orthographic convention should govern ambiguous Latin sequences, and is there an existing exception lexicon for loanwords and proper nouns?
Is a neural fallback acceptable in the company's private cloud, or must the solution be purely deterministic for security or latency reasons?
